instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.title: Exact authored strings lack a localization contract

atoms.statement: Keyboard support, accessibility, IME, selection, caret, clipboard, and input correctness are elevated to acceptance level, but there are no named assistive technologies, platform matrices, semantic roles, focus-restoration rules, composition-event cases, large-input cases, or pass/fail oracles.
atoms.title: Accessibility and IME requirements are acknowledged but not falsifiable

atoms.statement: Incoming symlinks are copied without resolution while containment checks focus on the normalized target directory; the plan does not specify rejection or labeling of links that point outside the project, component-safe resolution, target-directory symlink policy, or race-resistant file-descriptor operations.
atoms.title: Symlink and path containment rules permit unresolved escape and race cases

atoms.statement: The operation can be canceled, can continue after item failures, can retry failed items, and may be a move, but the spec does not define the commit point, cleanup of partial destination data, source deletion ordering, persisted receipts, idempotent retry, or recovery after app/OS crash.
atoms.title: Cancel, partial failure, retry, and restart semantics are not one coherent transfer transaction

atoms.statement: One sentence says a buffer must never exceed 5 MB, while the same sentence exposes a Hard cap setting whose example range reaches 10 MB; no precedence resolves whether 5 MB is absolute or merely the default.
atoms.title: The immutable 5 MB cap contradicts the configurable 2-10 MB hard cap

atoms.statement: Max editor tabs is described as capping tabs and buffers in memory with LRU eviction, but no eligibility, prompt, pinning, snapshot, write-lock, multi-view, or failure rule prevents eviction from discarding unsaved or unreconciled state.
atoms.title: Tab LRU eviction does not protect dirty, locked, or recovery-bearing buffers

atoms.statement: Recovered remote-backed buffers are explicitly local-only, use exact banner copy, and must reconnect or revalidate the destination before save or flush can claim success.
atoms.title: Recovered remote edits cannot masquerade as a successful remote write

atoms.statement: Changed-on-disk is checked on focus or before Save, but no expected-version token or compare-and-swap write is required at the actual atomic replace; remote recovered buffers similarly lack a base revision and three-way conflict rule after revalidation.
atoms.title: Save conflict checks are vulnerable to a check-to-write race

atoms.statement: Both document and file-editor views become read-only while the agent writes, streaming updates still enter the shared buffer, and release restores normal behavior without creating another history branch.
atoms.title: Document-pane writing lock preserves the shared-buffer invariant

atoms.statement: The lock is tied to a status string and released when that status changes, but crash, disconnect, canceled worker, duplicate writer, stale event, and reconnect cases are unspecified, as are lock ownership and user recovery controls.
atoms.title: Writing lock has no lease, owner identity, stall recovery, or forced-release rule

atoms.statement: Annotations bind canonical source text and stale rendered-state mutation is explicitly rejected, while Send selection to chat remains adjacent composer state and does not mutate the buffer.
atoms.title: Stale rendered selections must fail instead of silently rebasing

atoms.statement: Open-file visibility is filtered by execution role and approval scope, but there is no rule for already-open tabs, buffers, recovery snapshots, undo history, clipboard, recent lists, indexes, previews, or notifications when access is revoked or a user changes.
atoms.title: Approval-scope revocation does not define cache and UI data lifecycle

atoms.statement: OpenArtifact resolves artifact_id and follows several linked reference families, but ordering, missing-link behavior, cycle detection, conflicting envelopes, authorization checks at each hop, and content-hash revalidation are unspecified.
atoms.title: Artifact envelope traversal has no precedence, cycle, or stale-reference rules

atoms.statement: Mentions preserve canonical file identity and are project-scoped, yet the picker contract does not explicitly include worktree_id, execution_role, approval_scope, remote-cache state, or mixed-root disclosure even though open-file and worktree rules require those distinctions elsewhere.
atoms.title: Mention picker does not explicitly inherit worktree and approval visibility filters

atoms.statement: Markdown, Mermaid, HTML, SVG, image, and generated-document previews share identity, but this owner text defines no script policy, CSP/sandbox, local-file/network access, SVG external references, sanitization, decoder limits, navigation prompts, or trust labeling for untrusted workspace and artifact content.
atoms.title: Rendered preview inputs lack sandbox and resource-access requirements

atoms.statement: The PM-native target set is exact, system-default is a separate future handoff, and browser/terminal entrypoints remain placement and routing affordances rather than FileManager-owned runtime sessions.
atoms.title: Open targets and adjacent runtime owners are sharply bounded

atoms.statement: Open and route failures are logged and surfaced, but the required record shape omits operation IDs, retry attempt counts, timing, endpoint/cache/version context, redaction rules, user-copy-to-support data, and retention, making cross-surface diagnosis non-deterministic.
atoms.title: Operational failures lack correlation, redaction, and support diagnostics

atoms.statement: The continuation distinguishes FileManager rendering/routing from Search regex acceleration, LSP symbol data, FileSafe mutation safety, and Source Control git-native ownership, including correction of a stale Go-to-symbol owner reference.
atoms.title: Search, symbol navigation, diff, and Source Control ownership are explicit

atoms.statement: F-002 names the owned user-facing surfaces and explicitly defers chat UX, layout, browser actions, and storage terms to their owner documents.
atoms.title: F-002 preserves FileManager scope and owner deferrals

atoms.statement: Detection/import, override UI, indexing degradation, remote attachment, lazy loading, and performance are one split-recommended unit with empty dependency metadata and provenance-only validation, leaving sequencing and independently testable outcomes to builders.
atoms.title: F-003 compresses several independently failing subsystems without dependencies or acceptance oracles

atoms.statement: The unit bundles local-first remote operation, scanning, preview, recovery, widgets, Rust core, atomic save, watchers, and histories under lineage labels without measurable startup, memory, latency, crash, data-loss, or compatibility thresholds.
atoms.title: F-004 research constraints are broad but operationally unfalsifiable

atoms.statement: The unit rejects ephemeral state, weak recovery, limited workspace models, and terminal ownership, but does not translate those archetype-level concerns into durable-storage, reconnect, workspace-count, synced-scroll, sanitization, or ownership acceptance criteria.
atoms.title: F-005 archetype prohibitions lack concrete invariants

atoms.statement: The unit covers selection, caret, split-pane undo behavior, degraded language fallback, and editor updates—directly user-visible interaction and state—yet gui_related is false and the reason claims it has no GUI presentation.
atoms.title: F-006 is incorrectly marked non-GUI despite user-visible input and pane behavior

atoms.statement: Their repeated acceptance criteria prove source preservation and PlanUnit addressability, while validation surfaces run migration/index checks; no scenario, state transition, error injection, UI assertion, security test, or performance threshold demonstrates the canonical behavior.
atoms.title: F-002 through F-006 acceptance criteria validate migration form, not product behavior

atoms.statement: The unit explicitly centralizes Buffer, Tab, Editor group, Dirty, Preset, redb, seglog, and FileSafe terms, with an owner note separating seglog and FileSafe responsibilities.
atoms.title: F-007 establishes the local vocabulary

atoms.statement: The unit's save/history/undo authority determines visible editor behavior, and its source span explicitly carries requested-versus-effective editor modes, yet gui_related is false; this also risks separating transaction implementation from its required GUI state projection.
atoms.title: F-008 is marked non-GUI despite directly governing undo and visible effective modes

atoms.statement: The unit covers listing, open routing, virtualization, persisted expansion, ignored-file and row-cap settings, plus open, refresh, empty, and permission states.
atoms.title: F-009 preserves core tree behavior and explicit failures

atoms.statement: The unit retains project, repository, path, left/right worktree, and optional revision identity while forbidding a normal tab from hiding save/watch/undo/chat/diff identity.
atoms.title: F-010 makes cross-worktree compare identity explicit

atoms.statement: The unit bundles docking, filtering, ignored styling, menus, selection, validation, reveal, and keyboard accessibility without defining tree roles, focus transfer after pop-out/redock, selection announcement, menu traversal, high-contrast state, or keyboard-equivalent acceptance cases.
atoms.title: F-011 says keyboard accessibility but provides no interaction-state oracle

atoms.statement: The PlanUnit accurately carries copy-default and Shift-move behavior but does not add the confirmation, external-source policy, completion acknowledgement, or rollback contract necessary for the destructive move branch.
atoms.title: F-012 preserves Shift-move without resolving external deletion authority

atoms.statement: The unit mandates background progress/cancel alongside target validation and overwrite handling, yet its criteria and negative constraints say only that the UI thread must not block; they do not define safe points, destination cleanup, source deletion, or completion reporting after cancel.
atoms.title: F-013 requires cancel but not cancellation semantics

atoms.statement: The source says tree-open behavior requires the open-file contract and project context, while drag/drop relies on FileSafe and shared path rules, but every unit declares depends_on and unblocks empty; compilation therefore cannot enforce the documented prerequisites.
atoms.title: F-009 through F-013 erase explicit sequencing behind empty dependency arrays

atoms.statement: The accepted unit names path limits, disk space, cancellation, rollback, permissions, locked files, symlinks, and background execution, but does not define preflight timing, cleanup guarantees, retry idempotency, move-source state, or per-platform pass/fail cases.
atoms.title: F-014 names many failure classes without defining their transactional outcomes

atoms.statement: The governing prose describes optional drag-to-another-folder move and explicitly keeps copy as default even on the same filesystem; F-015 instead says internal reorder for custom sort and same-filesystem move fallback, adds drag-to-chat/show-hidden concepts, and remains an accepted requirement despite its deferred owner note.
atoms.title: F-015 changes optional move semantics into custom-sort reorder and marks deferred work accepted

atoms.statement: The unit retains open, save, dirty/read-only, large-file, transient-state, empty-file, canonical-path, cursor/scroll, and highlight-setting requirements.
atoms.title: F-016 captures the editor MVP acceptance surface

atoms.statement: The prose requires reorder only if the design supports it, but F-017 states that placement supports reorder without retaining the condition, so the PlanUnit changes product scope rather than preserving it.
atoms.title: F-017 strengthens optional tab reorder into unconditional support

atoms.statement: Dirty, read-only, degraded, marker, lock, stale-disk, changed-on-disk, transient failure, and recovery attention are not collapsed into one vague status; save failure preserves dirty state and recovery actions.
atoms.title: F-018 keeps save-related facts orthogonal

atoms.statement: The unit includes Restore to… / History and document-pane restore behavior that must be launched and observed in GUI surfaces, yet gui_related is false; this can exclude required GUI state, confirmation, error, and focus behavior from GUI planning.
atoms.title: F-019 is marked non-GUI despite defining visible restore actions

atoms.statement: The unit correctly forbids claiming remote success from local recovery, but does not bind the snapshot to a remote base revision or define the UI and data outcome when revalidation finds the destination changed, deleted, read-only, or moved.
atoms.title: F-020 requires revalidation but not remote conflict resolution

atoms.statement: The live action is exactly Work offline (cached files only), the shorthand is compatibility-only, no-cache state must disable or disclose, and disconnected listings/search/diff/git/shell/LSP/write capabilities cannot present as live.
atoms.title: F-021 fixes the offline label and prevents pretend-live remote surfaces

atoms.statement: The detailed source says the range highlight clears on edit or cursor movement, can fade after a configurable delay, and may disclose EOF clamping; F-022 compresses this to highlight/clamp support without preserving lifecycle, announcement, focus, reduced-motion, or color-independent acceptance requirements.
atoms.title: F-022 drops navigation-highlight lifecycle and accessibility behavior

atoms.statement: Each editor group has its own tab list and active tab, open defaults to the focused group, the file buffer is shared, and cursor/scroll state is per view.
atoms.title: F-023 preserves split-group view and buffer ownership

atoms.statement: The unit combines shared-buffer authority, read-only lock projection, banner, and streaming updates, but provides no lock token, writer identity, heartbeat, disconnect state, timeout, cancel, retry, takeover, or rollback behavior when streaming stops mid-write.
atoms.title: F-024 has no recovery path for a stale or failed writer lock

atoms.statement: Annotations, Send selection to chat, composer-prep state, and explicit stale-selection failure are direct GUI interactions and feedback, yet gui_related is false and the classification says this is only a state boundary.
atoms.title: F-025 is incorrectly classified non-GUI

atoms.statement: One buffer and dirty model is retained, Revert prompts before discard, and a dirty plus changed-on-disk condition must be one combined Reload/Overwrite/Cancel prompt rather than two sequential dialogs.
atoms.title: F-026 gives dirty plus changed-on-disk one explicit decision

atoms.statement: Per-buffer undo, clipboard, wrap/font, UTF-8, line endings, explicit Save, binary/read-only handling, and visible reason strings remain in the PlanUnit, with no autosave and no MVP hex view.
atoms.title: F-027 preserves explicit-save and read-only reason behavior

atoms.statement: Every unit repeats source-preservation acceptance and migration/index validators while depends_on/unblocks remain empty, despite remote, LSP, shared-buffer, document-pane, chat, storage, and watcher seams; no executable oracle proves the user-visible or failure behavior.
atoms.title: F-021 through F-027 remain provenance-valid but behavior-unverified and dependency-free
